programmes.t: Robbie Coltrane's Critical Evidence: Bodies Of Evidence: Roger Severs
programmes.d: In November 1993, Derek and Eileen Severs disappeared without a word. When police spoke to their son, Roger, he insisted they were on holiday. However, there was no evidence of this apparent trip, and Roger was soon arrested on suspicion of murder.

programmes.t: Robbie Coltrane's Critical Evidence: Resolution To Kill: Colin Ireland
programmes.d: In the summer of 1993 a serial killer stalked London. The Metropolitan Police investigated a bizarre murder in which a man was found naked on his bed with a dead cat draped over him. He’d been strangled and his flat had been wiped of evidence.

programmes.t: Killer Britain: Vincent Tabak
programmes.d: When landscape architect Joanna Yeates disappeared after work Christmas drinks, the nation was gripped by the search for her. Tragedy struck on Christmas day morning when her body was found in a snow-covered lane. But who had killed the young woman

programmes.t: Killer Britain: Peter Morgan
programmes.d: Millionaire Peter Morgan moved a young mother, Georgina Symonds, into one of his properties, paying her thousands a month to be his ‘girlfriend’. But when the relationship turned sour, he began plotting his revenge.

programmes.t: Killer Britain: Sabrina Kouider
programmes.d: Sabrina Kouider couldn’t have lived such a glamorous lifestyle without the help of Sophie Lionnet, the young French au pair who looked after her children. What Sophie didn’t know was that her employer was gripped by frenzied delusions and paranoia.

programmes.t: Killer Britain: Levi Bellfield
programmes.d: For years police suspected Levi Bellfield of crimes including sexual assault, GBH and abduction, but there was never enough evidence to charge him. Then they began connecting him with the murders of young blonde women.

programmes.t: Killer Britain: Lewis Daynes
programmes.d: Breck Bednar was a loving, family-oriented 14-year-old who had lots of friends and excelled at school. But he was also seduced by the world of online gaming. He didn’t see the dangers when an older teen made lucrative job offers.

programmes.t: Faces Of Evil
programmes.d: In the late 1980s, the community of Sacramento, California, is shaken by the discovery that a serial killer has been living in their midst. Beneath the grandmotherly exterior of Dorothea Puente, a seemingly kind landlady, lurks a chilling secret.

programmes.t: Faces Of Evil
programmes.d: Southern California was gripped by fear as a string of brutal murders left authorities baffled. Patrick Kearney, later dubbed the 'Trash Bag Killer', preyed on young men, luring them with his wicked charm before committing horrific acts of violence.

programmes.t: Faces Of Evil
programmes.d: Phillip Austin, once seen as an ordinary husband and father, shockingly slaughtered his wife, two children, and even the family dogs in an act of unimaginable violence.

programmes.t: Faces Of Evil
programmes.d: In the 1980s, Kansas City was gripped by terror as young men began to vanish without trace. Robert Berdella hid a gruesome secret: his home was a den of torture where his victims were subjected to unimaginable suffering before he murdered them.

programmes.t: Faces Of Evil
programmes.d: In October 1986, Brighton was gripped by fear after two young girls were found murdered in woods. Despite being arrested, Russell Bishop shockingly evaded justice due to a lack of evidence and went on to attack another young girl.

programmes.t: Faces Of Evil
programmes.d: In 1989, the town of Billingham was stunned by the brutal murder of Julie Hogg, whose body was found hidden in her home. Prime suspect Billy Dunlop was acquitted due to lack of evidence, exploiting the law of double jeopardy to evade justice.

programmes.t: Killer Britain
programmes.d: Nathan Maynard Ellis and David Leelsey shared a love of the macabre - their home was a shrine to horror. Maynard Ellis had long fantasised about turning fiction into fact. When he met the unsuspecting Julia Rawson, her fate was sealed.

programmes.t: Killer Britain
programmes.d: He started out as a peeping Tom, but Pawel Relowicz’s appetites grew. He was a sex pest who preyed on young women, and when Libby Squire was drunk and alone, he stalked her... and pounced.

programmes.t: Killer Britain
programmes.d: Mark Jewitt was a man with issues. Depressed and isolated, he grew obsessed with the noise that came from the flat downstairs. Jewitt was a time bomb, and the night that Vera Hudson forgot her keys, he went off.

programmes.t: Crimes That Shook Britain: The Murder Of Jill Dando
programmes.d: Documentary examining the unsolved murder of British TV presenter and newsreader Jill Dando, who was shot outside her house in Fulham, London, in 1999.

programmes.t: Crimes That Shook Britain: The Dunblane Massacre
programmes.d: In an emotional tribute, witnesses and victims' relatives look back on the tragic murder of 16 children and a teacher at Dunblane Primary School in Scotland, 15 years ago.

programmes.t: Crimes That Shook Britain: Jeremy Bamber
programmes.d: An investigation into Jeremy Bamber's brutal murder of his family in Essex, which occurred in 1985. Sentenced for life, he still maintains he is innocent. Is the right person behind bars?

programmes.t: Crimes That Shook Britain: The Murder Of Rhys Jones
programmes.d: The parents of innocent 11-year-old Rhys Jones, shot on his way home from a football club in Liverpool 2007, speak about the harrowing day when they lost their son.

programmes.t: Crimes That Shook Britain: The Murder Of Stephen Cameron
programmes.d: Gripping documentary examining the fatal stabbing of 21-year-old motorist Stephen Cameron during a motorway altercation in 1996.

programmes.t: Crimes That Shook Britain: Garry Newlove
programmes.d: Garry Newlove’s wife Helen talks about the events on the night of his murder and the days afterwards, as well as her current work as a peer in the House of Lords combatting anti-social behaviour.

programmes.t: Robbie Coltrane's Critical Evidence: Little Miss Nobody: Alan Charlton
programmes.d: An old carpet dug up by workmen in a Cardiff back garden in 1989 was the beginning of a case that would push the boundaries of forensic science. The carpet contained human bones - but whose?

programmes.t: Robbie Coltrane's Critical Evidence: The Perfect Murder: Roger& David Cooper
programmes.d: Robbie Coltrane examines the case of two brothers who murdered a marketing manager on Christmas Eve 2014 using chloroform.

programmes.t: Robbie Coltrane's Critical Evidence: Appointment With Death: Scott Singleton
programmes.d: Robbie Coltrane examines the case of Scott Singleton, who murdered a 17-year-old girl after luring her to a bogus job interview.

programmes.t: Robbie Coltrane's Critical Evidence: Countryside Killings: Graham Backhouse
programmes.d: Robbie Coltrane examines why Graham Backhouse attempted to kill his wife with a car bomb before murdering his neighbour in 1984.

programmes.t: Robbie Coltrane's Critical Evidence: Far From Home: Kyu Soo Kim
programmes.d: Robbie Coltrane examines the harrowing case of a London landlord who sadistically tortured and murdered two of his tenants.

programmes.t: Robbie Coltrane's Critical Evidence: The Saturday Night Strangler: Joe Kappen
programmes.d: In 1973, three young girls were beaten, raped and strangled over a six-week period. The Saturday Night Strangler escaped justice for almost 30 years. But new techniques in DNA technology and a midnight exhumation finally uncovered the killer.

programmes.t: Robbie Coltrane's Critical Evidence: The Double Axe Murderer: Dennis Smalley
programmes.d: A double axe murderer and no clues - except tiny flakes of paint discovered deep in the wounds of one of the victims. This is a story of how forensic science - and the determination of one detective - found the killer.
